data.name: Abedin
data.gender_notes: Abedin is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Abedin is of Arabic origin and is derived from the Arabic word ‘Abd’ meaning ‘servant’ or ‘slave’ and ‘Allah’ meaning ‘God’. The name Abedin thus signifies a servant or slave of God. In Islamic tradition, the term ‘Abd’ is used to denote a devoted and obedient servant of God. The name Abedin carries the meaning “Servant of God” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Abedin usually hope their child will grow to embody servant of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder to always serve and obey God.
data.etymology: Abedin belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Servant of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Abedin total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: While the term 'servant' or 'slave' may carry negative connotations in some cultures, the Islamic name Abedin carries a positive and noble meaning. In Islam, the idea of being a servant or slave of God is a source of pride and honor reflecting one's dedication, obedience, and submission to the divine will. This is evident in the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) statement, "The most beloved to me and closest to me are those who have the best manners and constancy in obeying Allah." (Sahih Bukhari)
